extracted.intended_audience: naval postgraduate students, DoD acquisition analysts, and government managers conducting OMB A-76 cost comparisons
extracted.subtask_description: A master's thesis evaluating whether an in-house Navy management information system (HRMIN) complies with OMB Circular No. A-76 by performing a cost comparison between in-house performance and contract-out alternatives and recommending whether conversion is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with OMB Circular No. A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain the compliance of this in‑house development with the Office of Management and Budget policy on the acquisition of commercial or industrial products and services needed by the government (OMB Circular No. A‑76).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report's purpose is to determine whether the in‑house HRMIN development follows OMB A‑76 acquisition policy. Implicit guidance: follow the procedures and standards described in Circular A‑76 when evaluating procurement/acquisition choices (i.e., use prescribed cost comparison methods and policy tests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison of in‑house performance vs contract‑out
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost comparison of the in‑house performance cost and the contract‑out cost of providing the services required of HRMIN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a side‑by‑side accounting of costs for in‑house operation and the anticipated contract costs for equivalent services. Use this quantitative comparison to judge which alternative is more cost effective; the thesis reports that the present in‑house performance is the most cost effective alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation tied to cost‑effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation on whether to convert to contracted‑out performance should be based on the cost comparison results (i.e., conversion should not be undertaken if in‑house is more cost effective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision rule applied: if in‑house performance demonstrates lower total cost (or better cost‑effectiveness) than contracting out, then do not convert. The report concludes conversion should not be undertaken because in‑house was most cost effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of system provenance and report metadata / release compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Document that the system was conceived and developed in‑house and include required thesis/report metadata (advisor, degree grantor, collection identifiers) and distribution statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record notes the development origin (Navy Military Personnel Command and NPRDC), advisor, degree details, collection (Naval Postgraduate School), identifiers (handle/ark), and distribution statement ('Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited'). For government reports/theses, include provenance and release/rights information (e.g., U.S. Government work status).
